# Expected values for lm_math_fi_pkg.f_lm_quantize, replayed by
# sim/generic_domain/tb_quantize_vectors.vhd.
#
# PURPOSE
#   Pins the arithmetic of f_lm_quantize for every legal combination of its
#   rounding and overflow arguments, so that a future edit to the function -
#   including one made while adding a new generic-domain check - cannot change
#   the result for a legal configuration without failing the gate.
#
# HOW THESE WERE PRODUCED
#   Emitted by simulating the version of src/lm_math_fi_pkg.vhd at commit
#   07345f1bc07a (the tip of main before the generic-domain work) under GHDL, and
#   calling f_lm_quantize once per combination. The generating package was
#   compiled into a separate library so the pre-change and post-change versions
#   could be compared side by side; that differential run reported all 4608
#   combinations bit-identical. These are therefore the pre-change values, and
#   the committed gate replays them against whatever the package does now.
#
#   Regenerating them is a deliberate act: it re-baselines the arithmetic. Do it
#   only when a behaviour change is intended, and say so in the changelog.
#
# COVERAGE
#   all 64 values of a 6-bit input
#     x 2 source signednesses   (C_LM_UNSIGNED = 1, C_LM_SIGNED = 2)
#     x 2 target signednesses
#     x 9 rounding modes        (C_LM_TRUNC_BITS = 0 .. C_LM_ROUND_AWAY = 8)
#     x 2 overflow modes        (C_LM_SATURATE = 1, C_LM_WRAP = 2)
#   = 4608 vectors. The four alias constants share a value with one of the nine
#   rounding modes, so they are covered by the value they alias.
#
# FORMAT
#   Lines beginning with '#' are comments. The first data line is the geometry:
#     old_width old_binpnt new_width new_binpnt
#   Every later line is one vector:
#     value old_arith new_arith rounding overflow expected_raw
#   where value and expected_raw are unsigned integer renderings of the input
#   and output bit patterns.
